answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: each agent's influence equals its account age times the number of honest epochs it has completed, recorded on a public ledge that all agents audit. Reputation accrues like a tide, rising only through repeated verified cooperation, so a fresh identity starts near zero and cannot fast-track. An attacker must keep thousands of sock puppets alive and honest for months, paying storage, fees, and opportunity cost, while each detection event wipes the account back to an oasis of nothing, making mass fakes economically pointless.
